note.explanation: Metabolism includes all the chemical reactions that keep an organism alive. Catabolism breaks complex molecules into simpler ones and releases energy. Anabolism builds complex molecules from simpler ones and uses energy.
examples: Cellular respiration breaks glucose into carbon dioxide and water to get energy.
Photosynthesis joins carbon dioxide and water to make glucose using sunlight.
note.checkAnswer: Anabolism requires energy input; photosynthesis is an example.
note.simple: Catabolism breaks things down and releases energy. Anabolism builds things up and needs energy.
note.checkQuestion: Which type of metabolism builds complex molecules and uses energy?
note.title: Metabolism: breaking down and building up
steps: Identify whether complex molecules are being broken down or built up.
If they are broken down into simpler ones, the process is catabolism and releases energy.
If simpler molecules are joined to form complex ones, the process is anabolism and consumes energy.
note.answer: Metabolism is the sum of all chemical reactions that occur within an organism to sustain life.

explain.title: Metabolism
explain.body: Metabolism is the sum of all chemical reactions that occur within an organism to sustain life. It has two subsets: catabolism and anabolism.

explain.title: Catabolism
explain.body: Catabolism involves the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler ones, releasing energy in the process. Cellular respiration and lipolysis are examples.

explain.title: Anabolism
explain.body: Anabolism involves building up complex molecules from simpler ones. This process consumes energy. Photosynthesis and protein synthesis are examples.

mistakes: Do not reverse the definitions: catabolism breaks down, while anabolism builds up.
Do not say that anabolism releases energy; it consumes energy.
When giving an example, make sure it matches the process: lipolysis is catabolism, while protein synthesis is anabolism.
Include the energy change as well as the change in molecules when differentiating the two processes.
